ir_definition_ref: p.5 (only informal remark: 'the largest class is over 40 times bigger than the smallest one' for ann)

outcome.smote_name_as_printed: not stated in paper (SMOTE only cited, Chawla et al. 2002, p.1/p.5)

chosen.condition: pure class-imbalance learning: equal misclassification costs, rescaling by reciprocal class sizes (eps_ij = 1/n_i), 10 imbalanced data sets, ten times 10-fold CV

summary_rows.label: pairwise two-tailed t-test 0.05, RESCALEnew vs BLIND (text p.5-6)
summary_rows.proposed: significantly better on 6 (abalone, ann, cmc, page, satellite, solarflare2), worse on 2 (car, connect4), no significant difference on 2 (balance, splice)

win_claim.quote: this paper shows that the proposed approach is helpful when unequal misclassification costs and class imbalance occur simultaneously, and can also be used to tackle pure class-imbalance learning.

uncertain: Chosen table: Table 6 (MAUC, vs BLIND) chosen by metric priority (AUC-type) and imbalance relevance; the paper's main comparator OLD appears only in cost-ratio Tables 3/4 (p.4), not in Table 6 (p.5).
source_repo 'UCI' for the 14 non-synthetic sets inferred from '14 UCI data sets and 6 synthetic data sets' (p.4); paper does not list per-dataset sources.
how_obtained 'not stated' for all UCI sets: no preprocessing described; class counts for abalone (3) and solarflare2 (6) may reflect author grouping but paper does not say (Table 2, p.4).
Bold marks read from rendered page image of Table 6 (p.5); text extraction lost bold.
notes: Proposed method: RESCALEnew (denoted NEW): checks cost-matrix consistency (rank of coefficient matrix < c); if consistent, solves weights w and rescales all classes via example weighting; otherwise pairwise-coupling decomposition with voting. Classifier C4.5 throughout. Tables 3 (consistent cost matrices) and 4 (inconsistent) on p.4 report misclassification cost on all 20 data sets: BLIND as absolute cost, OLD and NEW as ratios to BLIND (lower is better); e.g. Table 3 imbalanced ave. OLD .930 ± .066, NEW .867 ± .087; Table 4 imbalanced ave. OLD .925 ± .101, NEW .893 ± .161. Table 5 (p.5) W/T/L (t-test 0.05): NEW vs OLD 13/7/0 on CCM, 13/6/1 on ICM; NEW vs BLIND 15/5/0 (CCM), 17/2/1 (ICM); OLD vs BLIND 8/12/0 (CCM), 7/13/0 (ICM). Cost matrices randomly generated in [1,10] (smallest-to-largest class misclassification cost biggest for imbalanced sets). SMOTE is not evaluated. Pages: PDF index 1-6 = printed 567-572.
